name: Audience iframe
summary: How to build the audience-facing iframe of a slide-type plugin — mobile-first single-column layout, theme-from-xprops, self-rendered submit/waiting/correct-incorrect states, the standard submit-button spec, and host-utility integration — composed from existing components.
highlights: How to build the audience-facing iframe of a slide-type plugin
Mobile-first single column, theme from xprops, self-rendered states
Standard submit-button spec and host-utility integration
lead: The audience iframe is the phone-side counterpart to the presenter canvas: a separate entry, loaded at its own route, rendered mobile-first in its own cross-origin document. It ships NO new component — it reuses Button, Checkbox and Icon, paints with the deck palette / textColour / fontFamily the host forwards via window.xprops, and bundles semantic state colours from the design-system package because no --aha-* vars cross the iframe boundary. The narrative 'why', the worked BAD/GOOD examples and the C1..C22 judge criteria live in the DS `audience` guide; this artifact carries only the enforceable construction rules.

skillRef.note: This guide is the source of truth for rationale, worked BAD/GOOD examples, the AHAM-xxx bug references, and the full C1..C22 judge criteria plus the pre-ship checklist. This pattern distils the enforceable construction subset and links each rule back by ref (the judge's C-criteria, or a section label where the skill states a rule the judge doesn't separately enumerate).

surfaceChoice.useFor: most slide types — host paints the question image, title, description, audio button and countdown above your iframe; your iframe owns the answer area only
surfaceChoice.example: poll options, quiz answers, scale slider, word-cloud input

surfaceChoice.useFor: a slide needing a bespoke header the host chrome can't give — you render the whole surface including the title
surfaceChoice.example: intro slide, branded reveal, fullscreen quote

composedOf.use: the standard submit button — on the Developer Platform <aha-audience-submit> (wraps <aha-button variant="primary" size="touch" block>) from lib/audience.js (the iframe loads it), coloured by --aha-color-primary = the deck accent; a built plugin without the package rebuilds the same spec (full-width, ~44–48px, deck-accent fill, contrast-picked ink, disabled/submitting/locked/post-submit states)

multi-select option rows — the checked accent takes the deck accent (presentationColorPalette[0]), never Ant's fixed purple (you rebuild it in-iframe; the host AhaCheckbox does not cross the boundary)
open-ended / idea text with a character counter — <aha-counted-textarea size="touch"> from lib/audience.js on the Developer Platform, never a ported copy
single-line answers and names — <aha-counted-input size="touch"> (56px, 16px text; type="number" for a number) inside <aha-audience-field> from lib/audience.js on the Developer Platform
idea tags on the presenter side — <aha-tag> from lib/audience.js; on the audience phone a tappable chip is <aha-audience-chip> (44px, deck surface), never the 20px tag
the non-colour state cue paired with every colour signal — ✓ on submit, ✗ incorrect, lock icon on closed, leader trophy (glyph choice / size / stroke per the `icons` guide)
a stage / round indicator (Ideas → Group → Vote) — <aha-stepper>, current stage in ink (size="lg" on the canvas), never hand-rolled .step pills and never the primary accent
a type-to-pick field (owner, name, tag) — <aha-autocomplete>, never a hand-rolled <input> + <ul> combobox

the deck accent — presentationColorPalette[0] set on :root with the --aha-button-primary-* hover / press / text tokens, identical to the canvas; selected chips, checked controls and the submit button all read it
the one fixed dark ink (#1A1A1A) — never #1A1A2E and never a second near-black such as #000 for a dark label

16px — primary copy and option labels. --aha-size-sm is 12px (help / caption only) and --aha-size-default is 14px (secondary metadata), so 'text-sm 14px' maps to --aha-size-default, never --aha-size-sm
the correct / submitted / success function colour — bundled into the plugin build, never derived from the deck palette or a lookalike accent
the incorrect / validation-error / destructive function colour — bundled into the plugin build
caution / are-you-sure prompt body — bundled into the plugin build
informational note — bundled into the plugin build
a lone radio group that is not an answer (rare on the phone) — <aha-radio>; answer rows are always <aha-answer-list>, never radios laid out by hand

single- and multi-select option rows — <aha-answer-list> (rows: <aha-answer-option>); the checked control takes the deck accent, my pick is ringed in textColour, and lock-key keeps the pick across an iframe remount
scale input — <aha-scale-slider>: rail flush with min/max labels, rail and filled portion both ink 10% with a 1px ink-10% hairline
the deck-ink label above a DS field — <aha-audience-field> around <aha-counted-textarea size="touch"> (16px, dodges the iOS auto-zoom-on-focus), <aha-counted-input> or <aha-select>
the 'Submitted' announcement via the host's showToastSuccess — never an in-iframe banner (host paints it outside the iframe)
any modal interaction via the host's openPluginModal bottom-sheet — host paints the chrome, you fill the body
the neutral cold-start placeholder shown behind a themeReady guard while window.xprops populates
the ONE shared micro-instruction reused across every slide — <aha-instruction-line>, so the hint never drifts in size, weight or colour
the submit action with the busy, locked and closed states and the submission lock that survives an iframe remount
an ordering answer — <aha-rank-list>, live ordinal badges, keyboard move buttons and a pointer drag
a full-canvas slide's own timer — <aha-countdown> off the host's absolute end instant; a framed slide uses the host's timer instead
a participant photo — <aha-audience-image-upload>, the host uploads via xprops.uploadImage
the lobby / passive-phase screen — <aha-waiting-for-host>
the post-submit wait — <aha-submitted-card>
the "Submitting as" header when a round needs one — <aha-identity-strip>
a throw-to-answer card — <aha-swipe-card>
short tappable choices several to a line — <aha-audience-chip>

componentBacklog: composedOf marks 7 items this pattern leans on that the DS does not ship — the four semantic-state tokens (colorSuccess/Error/Warning/Info, which plugins bundle from the design-system package rather than read as --aha-* vars because no host CSS var crosses the iframe), plus toast, modal and skeleton (the first two are painted by the host outside the iframe). Radio, slider, textarea and the shared instruction now ship as the audience elements. Per the charter, a pattern leaning on a missing component is a signal to add it HERE.

rules.rule: Build the audienceUrl entry only — its own entry file, loaded at its own route, a separate document from the canvasUrl and editorUrl. Never branch one shared component with `if (audience) mobile else canvas`.
Lay out one vertical mobile-first column — question on top, answer area beneath, feedback after. No side-by-side panels. No horizontal scroll at any width; fit the narrowest phone (~320px).
Be fluid up to the host's max-width cap (~710–840px framed); don't set or fight the width.

Report content height via onHeightChange(h) on every size change so the host shrink-wraps the iframe. Use min-height for affordance and let content drive total height — no fixed pixel heights that assume a device.

Guard colour-bearing UI behind a themeReady check (!!textColour && palette.length > 0) and render a neutral color-mix skeleton while window.xprops loads — never flash hex-fallback colours that then switch to the real palette. The only sanctioned literals are #FFFFFF for the surface and 'Plus Jakarta Sans' for the font fallback.

Match the built-in type scale exactly: primary body copy, option labels and the submit-button label 16px (--aha-size-l); secondary metadata (vote-count chip, percentage, counter) 14px (--aha-size-default); help/caption 12px (--aha-size-sm — the token named 'sm' is 12px, not the 14px 'text-sm', so never use it for copy a participant must read); question/header 22px (host-painted in framed mode); form input 16px (dodges iOS auto-zoom); body line-height 1.5. Spacing on a multiple-of-8 rhythm (8/16/24).

onHeightChange reports the RESTING box. Keep any transform (swipe tilt, drag ghost, hover pop, settle bounce) small enough that its most-extreme frame's bounding box still fits the reported height; budget a little headroom rather than inflating the reported box. Prefer a cheap cap (e.g. 8° tilt over 12°).

Default is no inner scroll (let the host shrink-wrap). The one exception — a fixed-size bounded card (swipe/flash/reveal) — MAY scroll its own overflow with no page-level scroll, and MUST show a mask-image fade on the still-hidden edge(s), dropped when it all fits. Fade with CSS mask-image, never a coloured gradient overlay (no baseColour to match).

Keep a dragged/flung card at 60fps: drop expensive continuous effects (backdrop-filter, large box-shadow, any filter) while a `moving` flag is true and restore on settle; animate only transform/opacity (never width/height/top/left/margin); set will-change: transform.
Commit a swipe on EITHER the distance threshold OR a flick-velocity threshold (px/ms across pointermoves), so a fast flick flings instead of springing back.

Pull chart / visualization fills (bars, ring segments, plot dots, selection highlights) from xprops.presentationColorPalette (or presentationLighterColorPalette); pick the shade that contrasts against your chosen background.

State colours (submitted ✓, error ✗, correct/incorrect, warning, info) must NOT depend on the deck palette and must NOT come from --aha-* vars (they don't exist in this iframe). Bundle colorSuccess/colorError/colorWarning/colorInfo into the plugin build from the design-system package, so the audience sees the same success-green / error-red as the presenter canvas.

Use the actual function token (colorSuccess, colorError, colorWarning, colorInfo — all black #000000 under the 7 October 2026 colour rules) for state marks, and let the icon (✓ / ✗ / !) and wording carry the meaning, never a colour alone and never a lookalike accent (a teal such as #20E8B5 as a tick is wrong and fails contrast at ~1.58:1). On a dark deck put the black glyph on a bounded light fill (white badge), or a white glyph on a black pill.

Bind body text to xprops.slide.textColour. Do NOT use textColour as a border/divider/hairline source; derive hairlines from color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 10%, transparent) so they stay subtle and theme-aware.

No baseColour or backgroundImage is forwarded — choose your own background: a white / very light surface by default (works on light and dark decks), or derive a surface from the luminance of textColour.

fontFamily is only the font's NAME; this cross-origin iframe does not inherit the host's @font-face, so naming the family without loading the face renders all text in the serif fallback. Call useDeckFont(fontFamily) in THIS iframe (its own call — loading on the canvas does nothing here); defaults to 'Plus Jakarta Sans'.

A checked Radio/Checkbox, a selected chip and the submit fill take the deck ACCENT — presentationColorPalette[0] published as --aha-color-primary on :root (the same value the canvas uses; a local alias such as --aha-control-accent must be set from that same value) — never Ant's fixed colorPrimary purple and never a 'toward-ink' variant of it. The selected-answer ring/edge takes the deck's textColour so it stays visible on any deck; the accent still marks the pick on the control and in label weight.

Publishing the accent var is mandatory — something in the render tree must actually SET --aha-control-accent (inline style/:style on the control or an ancestor, from presentationColorPalette[0]). Referencing the var with only a purple fallback, without ever publishing it, ships purple on every deck.

Fill a slider/progress track with the deck ink at 10% and give a filled part the same 1px hairline (color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 10%, transparent)) so a coloured fill doesn't sink into a same-hue deck — one value for every audience border and track, no heavier 20% edge.
Zero out Ant's default slider margin (~margin: 10px 6px) so a horizontal slider's rail runs edge-to-edge, flush under the row holding its min/max end labels.

Distinct labelled sections sit ≥24px apart: wrap each section (label + its control) in its own tight flex-col gap-2 and space whole sections on the outer column with gap-6. The 8px gap is for rows INSIDE one group; don't stand a per-label mt-2/mt-3 in for a real section break.

Don't pair a pastel/tinted background with icon + text in the same hue (monotone 'AI' look). Bind ink to textColour (which tracks and contrasts), or pair a tint with genuinely high-contrast ink and clear hierarchy — not one hue at two brightnesses.

Rectangular content containers stay on the DS radius scale: cards and panels 12px (--aha-radius-lg, as the DS card measures), option tiles, inputs, the swipe card's inner tiles and the submit button 8px, and nothing above 12px — rounded-2xl/3xl (16/24) read toy-like, and the cap applies to the OUTER wrapper too. Intentionally circular elements (pills, chips, badges, avatars, dots, progress tracks) stay fully rounded.
Text weight is 400 or 600 only (the standard submit button is 600). No 700/800/900 (font-bold/extrabold/black) — heavy weight reads 'AI'.

Delete any label, header or divider that merely repeats an adjacent control — two labelled True/False buttons don't need a 'True or False' header or an 'OR' divider; the buttons are the prompt. A word earns its place only if it says something the controls don't.

A micro-instruction is the shortest possible phrase in the DEFAULT body (16px, regular 400, the deck's textColour) — never a pill, tinted card, shadowed chip or button-shaped box, and never semibold or muted-grey. Use ONE shared instruction component across every slide so it never drifts between slides.

Primary body copy and option labels stay at the audience default 16px (--aha-size-l), never text-sm. 14px (--aha-size-default) is legitimate ONLY on secondary metadata beside a label (vote-count chip, percentage, character counter) — never on the option label, a chip label, a tag or the question restatement. The token --aha-size-sm is 12px, so a builder who maps 'text-sm' to --aha-size-sm lands two pixels smaller still: map by pixel value, not by name.

Declare setting.enableFullScreen explicitly in the manifest — framed (default) for most types (host paints its chrome above the iframe), full-canvas only for a bespoke header. Never mix framed mode with your own title (it duplicates the host's).

The plugin self-renders every post-submission state inside the iframe (host shows no generic 'Waiting…' screen for plugins): just-submitted, waiting-for-next-slide (calm, no noisy spinner), quiz correct/incorrect (semantic colour + non-colour ✓/✗ cue + answer text, bar fills stay palette), and a pre-submission empty state (show the input affordance with placeholder copy, never a giant '0' or empty chart).
Keep state transitions smooth — re-report height via onHeightChange when a state change legitimately changes content height, but avoid layout jumps >16px between adjacent states.

Announce submission with xprops.showToastSuccess(t('audience.submitted')) — the host paints a consistent toast outside the iframe. Never re-implement a 'Submitted' banner inside the iframe; after the toast, transition content to results / quiz feedback / waiting.

Use the standard submit button: on the Developer Platform it is <aha-audience-submit> from lib/audience.js (it wraps <aha-button variant="primary" size="touch" block> and adds the busy, locked and closed states plus the submission lock; never a hand-ported copy of its CSS); a built plugin without the package rebuilds the same spec. Full-width block, ~44–48px tall, 8px corners, fill from the deck accent via --aha-color-primary (never a hard-coded brand colour, never a bare type="primary" fixed purple), readable ink chosen by fill luminance (white or #1A1A1A), semi-bold, positioned at the end of the answer area with ~16px below.

When input is invalid the submit button is a distinct NEUTRAL GREY surface (grey fill + grey text), not the coloured fill at reduced opacity (a dimmed purple still reads enabled). No pointer cursor; aria-disabled="true"; block submit until the user has picked/typed.
While submitting, show an inline spinner INSIDE the button — the button doesn't disappear, change height or move (no layout jump) — and lock it to prevent double-submit.
On host stopSubmission, swap to a locked state: lock icon + i18n 'submission closed' label replacing the submit label; the button stays present (no reflow) but uninteractive.

After submit completes: a scored quiz swaps to a circular badge — green ✓ correct / red ✗ incorrect using the bundled semantic colours; a non-scored slide fires showToastSuccess and transitions to the plugin-rendered submitted/waiting state.

Secondary actions (Skip, Start voting) use a lower-contrast variant (surface + border, or a desaturated palette shade), same height, same i18n discipline — the hierarchy must read clearly as primary vs side option. Never paint two visually equal buttons.
Call onSubmitButtonHeightChange(h) with the submit button's y-offset so the host can paint the floating 'Scroll to submit' pill when the button sits below the fold.

Put a kebab-case data-testid scoped to the slide type on every interactive element (e.g. audience-<slidetype>-submit-button, audience-<slidetype>-option-3) so QA can target it across slide types and releases.
Label every control via t(...) — never hard-coded 'Submit'/'Send'/'Vote'. All user-visible text translates per xprops.presentation.language.

Use the host utilities rather than reinventing them in-iframe: showToast* for transient feedback/errors, openPluginModal/closePluginModal for modals (host paints chrome, you fill the body), onSubmitButtonHeightChange for the sticky pill, scrollTo/getWindowHeight for positioning. Lean toward the utility so it stays consistent and host-evolvable.

In framed mode the host already paints the countdown progress bar above the iframe — do NOT duplicate it with your own pill/widget. Use xprops.timeLimit as LOGIC only (e.g. lock submit when timeLimit <= 0). In the rare full-canvas case, render the countdown bound to the live xprops.timeLimit, never static text or your own setInterval.

The host owns the countdown EXPIRY notice — it announces 'Time's up' in its chrome. Don't draw your own 'Time's up' / deadline card in the iframe (it double-announces and drifts from the host clock); let the round-end state you DO own carry the meaning.
Never write static time text ('30 seconds', '1 phút', 'đếm ngược 30s') anywhere — description, label or helper — it drifts from reality the moment the timer ticks.

Don't render or assume-broken host-owned layers: edge states (lost connection, poll closed, kicked, last slide, slide skipped) overlay from the host — don't draw your own; logo / watermark / branding / plan-gating are host layers; baseColour / backgroundImage never reach the iframe.

Locale is xprops.presentation.language (presenter's choice), not the audience browser — don't override, just translate. The host does not flip RTL by language; if your slide type needs RTL (Arabic, Hebrew) handle it yourself (dir="rtl" on the root, logical CSS).
Touch targets are roughly finger-sized (~44–48px, iOS 44pt / Android 48dp) as a recommended range; leave ≥8px between tappables to avoid mis-taps.

Meet WCAG AA against your CHOSEN background — 4.5:1 text, 3:1 large text and meaningful shapes — verified on both light and dark decks (since baseColour isn't forwarded, you make and defend the background choice).
Keep a visible focus ring — keyboard users on tablets/laptops still join; don't remove the default ring without replacing it.
Don't use motion alone to convey meaning — it's lost on bad connections and for prefers-reduced-motion users.
Pair a non-colour cue with every colour-bearing signal (state, error, correct/incorrect, leader) — prefer an icon (✓/✗) over a verbose word chip; it's compact and language-neutral.

Keep chart geometry honest — if a row has an indicator only sometimes (e.g. a leader trophy), reserve a fixed-width slot on every row so all bar tracks share width; a 55% bar must occupy 55%, not 48% because the chip ate the difference.

The iframe has its own i18n instance (not inherited from host): initialise locale from xprops.presentation.language with xprops.currentUser.presenterLanguage as fallback, and subscribe to host language changes mid-session.
Format numbers / percentages with Intl.NumberFormat(locale), not .toFixed(...) + '%' (some locales use ',' as the decimal separator).

On the Developer Platform the audience iframe loads lib/audience.js, so every control the DS ships is consumed as the element: the audience set (<aha-answer-list>, <aha-rank-list>, <aha-scale-slider>, <aha-audience-chip>, <aha-audience-field> around <aha-counted-input> / <aha-counted-textarea size="touch"> / <aha-select>, <aha-audience-image-upload>, <aha-audience-submit>, <aha-countdown>, <aha-instruction-line>, <aha-waiting-for-host>, <aha-submitted-card>, <aha-identity-strip>, <aha-swipe-card>; the Audience Library page maps each upstream component to its element) plus the shared ones (<aha-button>, <aha-stepper>, <aha-autocomplete>) — never 'ported 1:1' by copying its CSS, which freezes the copy at the version of the day it was built. Keep a control custom only where the DS has no element yet, and build it on DS tokens.

One accent per deck: presentationColorPalette[0] maps onto --aha-color-primary on the iframe's :root (with --aha-button-primary-bg-hover / -bg-press / -text), exactly as on the canvas, so the presenter and the participant see the same colour. Only the label ink is picked by contrast. Never reuse a semantic colour (success teal, error red) as a data or series colour.

Borders are hairlines: a bounded white card takes 1px --aha-border (#E3E3E3); a deck-owned surface (chip, field, track, dashed image drop zone) takes 1px color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 10%, transparent). Never a 2px outline at heavy ink (e.g. 55% textColour) on chips, cards or inputs.
One fixed dark ink on every surface: --aha-text-default #1A1A1A. Never the retired indigo #1A1A2E and never #000 for a dark label on the accent.

Every interactive state (hover, selected, pressed, expanded) animates with --aha-motion-* durations and --aha-ease-* curves on a PERSISTENT node — patch the DOM (toggle a class or attribute) instead of rebuilding with innerHTML on each update, which kills the transition. Respect prefers-reduced-motion; motion never carries meaning alone.

A stage indicator is <aha-stepper> and a type-to-pick field is <aha-autocomplete> (both in lib/audience.js); a sentiment glyph is the matching face (system-smiley / system-sad-face / system-angry-face). Never hand-roll stepper pills or a combobox, and never mark the current stage with the primary accent — the stepper marks it with ink so the accent stays on the one action that advances the flow.

reuseNote: Doc-only pattern — ships no composition wrapper from this repo. The audience-iframe building blocks (submit button, option rows, instruction line, skeleton, the xprops theme binding and useDeckFont helper) live in the slide-type-plugin repos and are painted from window.xprops per plugin; they are not importable across the cross-origin iframe boundary, and semantic state colours are bundled per-plugin from the design-system package. If a shared audience wrapper ever graduates into this DS, add a reuse block and it is gated like a composite.

selfCheck.label: single-column mobile-first, no horizontal scroll at ~320px; height via onHeightChange
colour/font from xprops; semantic state bundled (not --aha-*, not deck palette)
submit button matches spec + all states wired (disabled/submitting/locked/post-submit)
plugin self-renders submitted/waiting/correct-incorrect/empty; host utilities used, not reinvented
enableFullScreen declared; i18n from xprops.presentation.language; no static time text

primary copy 16px (--aha-size-l, not --aha-size-sm); one accent via --aha-color-primary; <aha-*> elements from all.js, no ported CSS; ink #1A1A1A; 1px borders, 12px cards; motion tokens on persistent nodes

whenToRead: ANY audience (phone) view of a slide type. Holds the 16px primary-copy rule (--aha-size-sm is 12px, so 16px maps to --aha-size-l), the one-accent rule shared with the canvas, <aha-*> elements from all.js on the Developer Platform instead of ported CSS, one dark ink #1A1A1A, 1px borders with 12px cards, and motion tokens on persistent nodes. Stage indicators are <aha-stepper> and type-to-pick fields <aha-autocomplete>, never hand-rolled.
